images.filename: Open stands of Corsican Pines - geograph.org.uk - 255682.jpg
images.caption: Open stands of Corsican Pines Corsican pines were first introduced to Newborough in 1948. Previous to that the sand dunes were covered with marram grass. This was gathered by the locals and formed the basis of a cottage industry manufacturing woven grass mats.
images.alt: Open stands of Corsican Pines Corsican pines were first introduced to Newborough in 1948. Previous to that the sand dunes were covered with marram grass. This was gathered by the locals and formed the basis of a cottage industry manufacturing woven grass mats.

images.filename: Flat open field to the north of Newborough-Niwbwrch - geograph.org.uk - 393089.jpg
images.caption: Flat open field to the north of Newborough/Niwbwrch Most of this square is rough grazing land to the east of the northern block of Newborough Forest.  It is part of the old (now drained) flood plain of the River Cefni.  Rising away in the background is one of the many ridges running NE/SW over the island parallel to the Menai Strait.
images.alt: Flat open field to the north of Newborough/Niwbwrch Most of this square is rough grazing land to the east of the northern block of Newborough Forest.  It is part of the old (now drained) flood plain of the River Cefni.  Rising away in the background is one of the many ridges running NE/SW over the island parallel to the Menai Strait.

images.filename: Looking WNW from junction of footpath and land-drain 3km north of Newborough-Niwbwrch - geograph.org.uk - 393148.jpg
images.caption: Looking WNW from junction of footpath and land-drain  3km north of Newborough/Niwbwrch This square is virtually completely flat with the land-drain as the only feature.  The land-drain is one of several in the area next to the Cefni which has helped turn the old flood plain into good grazing land.  In the background is Pen-y-bont farm and Malltraeth going up the hill on the other side of the Cefni.
images.alt: Looking WNW from junction of footpath and land-drain  3km north of Newborough/Niwbwrch This square is virtually completely flat with the land-drain as the only feature.  The land-drain is one of several in the area next to the Cefni which has helped turn the old flood plain into good grazing land.  In the background is Pen-y-bont farm and Malltraeth going up the hill on the other side of the Cefni.
